extracted.intended_audience: philosophers, scientists, and educated readers interested in philosophy of science and critique
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for judging philosophical doctrines, scientific theories, and critics' judgments — emphasising methodological consistency, the role of observation/experiment, logical clarity of definitions, and how to weigh errors in detail versus the unity of a theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate a critic by his general mental peculiarities
rubrics_metrics.description: One way of estimating the validity of a critic's judgments, is that of studying his mental peculiarities as generally displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If he betrays idiosyncrasies of thought in his writings at large, it may be inferred that these idiosyncrasies possibly, if not probably, give a character to the verdicts he passes upon the productions of others. (Used to motivate examination of Professor Tait's general habits of thought as a basis for judging his criticism.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Require experimental/observational justification for physical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no observation or experiment is possible, no physical truth can be established; in the absence of any possibility of experiment or observation there is no basis for any physical belief at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an implication of a strict experimentalist stance (attributed to Professor Tait). The author discusses limits when extending physical laws to realms where experiment/observation cannot be done (e.g., relation between visible and invisible universes), and flags this as a problematic implication if applied inconsistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency in epistemic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not apply the standard 'only experimental/observational justification counts' inconsistently — i.e., demand experiments for perceived phenomena but then reason physically about unperceived phenomena without experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticises Professor Tait for implicitly holding that physical axioms are knowable only by experiment, yet treating reasoning about the unseen universe as having physical validity. Consistency between one's stated standards and their applications is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer precision and logical consistency in definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions used in argument (e.g., 'force') must be clear and not self-contradictory; reconcile differing definitions rather than letting them produce paradoxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: contrasting definitions of force — 'that which changes the state of a body' (Newton) vs. 'the rate at which an agent does work per unit of length' — can produce a logical contradiction (treating a relation as an agent). Avoid such confusions; ensure terms function coherently within the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: To refute a comprehensive theory, attack its foundational premises or derivations
rubrics_metrics.description: If it can be shown that the Persistence of Force is not a datum of consciousness; or if it can be shown that the several laws of force are not corollaries from it; or if it can be shown that, given these laws, the redistribution of matter and motion does not necessarily proceed as described; then the theory will be undermined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lays out where a challenger must focus to shake a general theory — show foundational datum false, show claimed corollaries don't follow, or show derivations to concrete phenomena are invalid. Minor errors in illustration are insufficient to overturn the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate significance of core doctrine from errors in illustrative details
rubrics_metrics.description: The truth of the doctrine as a whole is unaffected by errors in the details of its presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author warns that alleged minor falsehoods in examples or illustrations do not necessarily impugn the general conclusion; critics should not assume that mistakes in peripheral propositions invalidate the central theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provisional assumptions and validate by congruity of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed with assumptions provisionally until they are proved true by the congruity of the results reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that analysis requires assumptions; the proper course is to treat them as provisional and accept them only insofar as the web of deductions and the congruity of outcomes support them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret phenomena as parts of broader processes for completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: All phenomena receive their complete interpretation only when recognized as parts of general processes (e.g., Evolution and Dissolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that partial sciences must be unified into a deductive interpretation from general laws (Persistence of Force) to yield total and specific interpretations of phenomena; completeness of explanation requires situating particulars within broader lawful processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dismissing complex formulations by mere caricature or mock-translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not render purposely vague or complex statements meaningless by mock translations or travesties; such surface ridicule does not substitute for substantive critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Professor Tait's parody ('no-howish, untalkaboutable...') of a definition of Evolution is shown as an instance of dismissive mockery rather than engagement. Critics should engage the intended meaning rather than reduce it to buffoonery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize neutrality of systematic reduction regarding metaphysical interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction of phenomena to simpler symbols (e.g., Matter, Motion, and Force) is methodologically neutral between materialist and spiritualist metaphysical conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes that correlation and equivalence between inner and outer forces can be used to support opposite metaphysical readings; thus scientific/systematic formulations do not by themselves decide ultimate metaphysical positions.
